notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase boundaries between course-start/during-work/general (e.g. whether a ban sentence is communicating expectations or governing the work) resolved by what the sentence governs; (2) sanction sentences ('will be considered academic dishonesty') coded must/neutral by one coder and informs/restrict by the other, resolved as binding consequence with no stance on AI use; (3) unit_stance require vs permit for citation conditions, resolved as permit since 'require' means AI use itself is required, and permit vs neutral for tool listings, resolved as neutral; (4) UNCOVERED vs stretched fit for the instructor-approval gate, closed task whitelist and pre-decision weighing of ethics, resolved toward UNCOVERED; (5) P12 vs P14 and P35 vs P40 for baseline writing samples. Both coders agreed on document stance (delegates) for all three documents. Units found by one coder only were all checked against the source and kept (A-only: 3+4+1, B-only: 4+1+0), mostly because the other coder merged two rules into one unit or skipped a sentence. Coder B's non-standard topic labels were replaced.
